rationale: The census holding is already represented by the existing single ArcLight Capital Partners ownership period, so the queued ADD_OWNER action must be suppressed. REC Solar nevertheless requires record-level corrections: the same operating platform rebranded as REC Power on 2026-06-30; its current website, headquarters and broader distributed-power scope should be recorded; ArcLight Fund VII is directly supported as the fund rather than as a legal acquisition vehicle; the platform-level acquisition vehicle and percentage stake are not publicly disclosed; exact announcement and closing dates should be added; and the unsupported 2025 dating of the scale milestone should be replaced with directly dated 2026 evidence.

identityResolution.headquarters: San Luis Obispo, California, United States
identityResolution.platformBoundary: One manager-level nationwide distributed-power independent power producer and operating platform, now publicly branded REC Power. It develops and acquires projects, finances them, and owns, operates and services distributed solar, battery-storage, fuel-cell, microgrid and genset assets. The platform is the continuing commercial REC Solar business after its residential division was sold to Sunrun in 2014, and it incorporates the commercial distributed-generation assets, pipeline, O&M portfolio and personnel transferred by Duke Energy in 2023. The former Duke portfolio, Bloom-managed fuel-cell assets, individual projects, project LLCs, tax-equity structures and intermediate holding entities are not separate manager-level PortCos. Current regulatory sources still use REC Solar Commercial Corporation for certain legal registrations; no direct source establishes a platform-wide corporate-name conversion to a newly incorporated REC Power legal entity.
identityResolution.duplicateDecision: NOT_DUPLICATE. Update existing production company ID cmrxpj6jr00jgivheinookosn in place. REC Power is the 2026 successor public name of REC Solar, not a second company, and the acquired Duke commercial distributed-generation portfolio is part of this platform rather than a second canonical PortCo.

acquisitionExitCheck.dukeOwnershipHistory: Duke Energy announced that it acquired a majority interest in REC Solar on 2015-02-09, acquired full ownership on 2017-12-06, and ceased to be an owner when the ArcLight transaction closed on 2023-10-04. Duke is a former corporate owner only and must not be mapped to an infrastructure-fund strategy or retained as a current owner.
acquisitionExitCheck.arcLightAnnouncement: On 2023-07-05, Duke Energy announced a definitive agreement to sell its commercial distributed-generation business to an affiliate of ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC for $364 million of enterprise value, inclusive of non-controlling tax-equity interests. The sold business included REC Solar operating assets, development pipeline and O&M portfolio, plus distributed fuel-cell projects managed by Bloom Energy; employees were to transition with the business.
acquisitionExitCheck.arcLightClosing: On 2023-10-04, Duke Energy announced completion of the sale to an investment fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners. That legal closing is the supported ArcLight entry date. The sources establish transfer of the broader commercial distributed-generation business and continuation of REC Solar as the operating platform, but do not disclose a platform-level percentage stake or name the contractual acquisition SPV.
acquisitionExitCheck.subsequentExitSearch: Targeted searches through 2026-08-15 for REC Solar or REC Power sales, exits, divestitures, mergers, dissolutions, restructurings, successor names and signed pending transactions found no PortCo-level exit or pending ownership transfer. ArcLight's current-investments table still lists REC Solar as Current, the 2026-06-30 rebrand release calls REC Power an ArcLight portfolio company, and the 2026-07-28 company release says REC Power is owned by ArcLight Capital Partners. DigitalBridge's 2026-05-27 signed agreement to acquire ArcLight itself remained contingent on the pending SoftBank/DigitalBridge transaction and other approvals; it is a manager-level transaction, not a disclosed transfer of the REC Power holding, and therefore does not create a pending PortCo owner row.

milestones.event: Judy Staley and Fred Sisson co-founded REC (Renewable Energy Concepts) Solar in California.

Sunrun acquired REC Solar's residential division; the commercial business continued independently under the legal name REC Solar Commercial Corp., establishing the boundary of the later Duke/ArcLight platform.
Duke Energy acquired a majority interest in REC Solar.
Duke Energy acquired full ownership of REC Solar.
Duke Energy announced the definitive sale agreement for its commercial distributed-generation business, including REC Solar, to an ArcLight affiliate.
Duke Energy completed the sale to an investment fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners; this is the ArcLight entry date.

REC Solar rebranded as REC Power, explicitly stating that the name changed while the company and customer commitment continued; the release described 700+ deployed projects and continued ArcLight backing.

REC Power completed the acquisition of fifteen operating distributed-generation solar projects totaling 68 MW, taking its operating portfolio above 410 MW across 25 states; the release directly stated that REC Power is owned by ArcLight Capital Partners.
